terms.gloss: the level sea; any level surface
evidence: Varr. LL 7.23: aequor mare appellātum, quod aequātum, cum commōtum ventō nōn est (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: From aequus, level: the plain of the sea when no wind stirs it, and so the sea. A poets’ word before Augustus; once in Cicero and once in Sallust (Lewis & Short).

evidence: Verg. A. 3.193: caelum undique et undique pontus (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Greek πόντος, the poets’ word for mare (Lewis & Short).

terms.register: vōx poētica: Lucr., Verg., Hor.; also post-Augustan prose
evidence: Verg. A. 5.8: pelagus tenuēre ratēs (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Greek πέλαγος; a neuter in -us.

phrases.english: sky on every side and on every side the sea
the ships held the open sea

sources: Lewis & Short: mare
